props.title: The Light Function

B09.capture_spec: C05: Dusk tiled floor, one warm lamp (scale 5) at the centre, the blob at (1250, 700). The floor starts on default lighting; at 'Even an empty one' it switches to 01-light-empty. The blob never changes. Scene = evidence/planning-checks/light_scene.gd with captures.json id C05; 1920 x 1080 window at scale 1, 30 fps, 16 s, Forward+. Expected: floor (1100, 540) = (1.000, 0.949, 0.824) before and (0.400, 0.427, 0.518) after (tile x dusk); blob centre (0.365, 0.616, 0.561) before and after (verify8 C05).
B09.visual_intent: Act title 'The Light Function' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the empty light() function and a definition tag on its first line ('light(): runs once per pixel for each light that touches it'); at right a real Godot window: the lit floor and the blob. At 'Even an empty one' the glow leaves the floor (only the dusk look is left) while the blob stays lit. A ring settles on the blob, labels 'default lighting' (blob) and 'empty light()' (ground).
B09.motion_claim: The glow vanishes from the floor but stays on the blob the instant the empty function is added.

show.event: empty function assigned: the glow leaves the ground
ring on the blob: still lit
code highlighted again: it belongs to the sprite

B09.why: The claim is a before and after on one picture, with the unchanged blob as the control; the code card is the cause.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · lamps switched on one by one · scripted

B10.capture_spec: C06: Dusk tiled floor with three warm lamps (scale 3.4, energy 0.4) stacked near the centre that switch on at 'Add a lamp', 'Add another' and 'once for each lamp'. A grey card (0.7, 640 x 400 px) at the centre wears 02-light-flat; the floor stays on default lighting. Scene = evidence/planning-checks/light_scene.gd with captures.json id C06; 1920 x 1080 window at scale 1, 30 fps, 14 s, Forward+. Expected: card at (700, 700): (0.349, 0.384, 0.502) with no lamp, then (0.549, 0.584, 0.702), (0.749, 0.784, 0.902), (0.949, 0.984, 1.000): +0.2 per lamp (verify8 C06).
B10.visual_intent: Code card at left with the flat light() (LIGHT = vec4(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1.0)); at right a real Godot window: a grey card on the dusk floor. Each lamp that switches on lifts the card by one more flat step, with no soft falloff, while the floor around it shows the lamps' soft glows. Readouts '+0.2', '+0.4', '+0.6'.
B10.motion_claim: The card brightens by the same step each time a lamp appears.
B10.why: Equal steps per lamp on a real card are the proof that the function runs once per lamp and the answers add.

B11.visual_intent: A box labelled light(). Four arrows come in from the left, labelled in monospace capitals COLOR, UV, LIGHT_COLOR, LIGHT_ENERGY; one arrow leaves to the right labelled LIGHT. Caption: 'built-in: a value the engine hands to a function, or collects from it'. A grey note: 'more in the docs: NORMAL, SCREEN_UV ...'.
B11.motion_claim: The four inputs slide into the box one after another and the single answer leaves on the right.
B11.why: The idea is values in and one value out; a box with arrows is exactly that, while the docs table has more rows than the voice can name.

B12.visual_intent: A strip left to right on the cream stage: 'fragment()  sets color' -> 'light()  once per lamp' (two small lamp dots feed it, each answer a small swatch) -> '+ dim ambient look' -> a pixel swatch. A token travels the strip; the arrows are drawn shapes pointing only forward.
B12.motion_claim: A token passes fragment, splits into one pass per lamp, and the answers join the ambient look to make the pixel.
B12.why: An order of work is a token moving forward through stages, never back.
